title: The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book 2, Fugue 17 in A-flat major

character.text: Triple-counterpoint fugue on a lament subject, in trio-sonata style

sections.label: Episode 1
sections.summary: Alto: a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times) and a figure from the subject. Tenor: a figure from the subject, inverted. Bass: a figure from the subject, inverted (7 times) and a figure from the subject, in a sequence rising by a step every half bar.

sections.label: Episode 2
sections.summary: Alto: free counterpoint. Tenor: a figure from the subject. Bass: a figure from the subject. Returns in Episode 6 (bars 39–40).

sections.label: Episode 3
sections.summary: Alto: a figure from the subject (2 times). Tenor: a figure from the subject. Bass: free counterpoint.

sections.label: Episode 4
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject, inverted (4 times) and a figure from the subject, in a sequence rising by a step every half bar. Alto: a figure from the subject, inverted (5 times) and a figure from the subject (4 times), in a sequence falling by a step every half bar. Bass: a figure from the subject, inverted (4 times) and a figure from the subject, in a sequence rising by a step every half bar.

sections.label: Episode 5
sections.summary: Soprano: free counterpoint. Alto: free counterpoint. Tenor: a figure from the subject (3 times).

sections.label: Link
sections.summary: Soprano: free counterpoint. Alto: free counterpoint. Tenor: a figure from the subject, inverted.

sections.label: Episode 6
sections.summary: Reworks Episode 2 (bars 15–16) in part, with the tenor's line in the bass, the bass's line in the soprano, the lines moved by different intervals (invertible counterpoint at the tenth). Soprano: a figure from the subject (2 times). Alto: a figure from the subject. Tenor: free counterpoint. Bass: a figure from the subject (2 times), in a sequence falling by a fourth every half bar.

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in A♭ major (Tenor); Answer in A♭ major (Bass)
Episode 7
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject (2 times). Alto: free counterpoint. Tenor: free counterpoint. Bass: a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times) and a figure from the subject.

spans.label: Codetta
spans.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject (2 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted. Alto: the opening of the subject.
